uncited: Camera and Projection Models define the geometric transformation from 3D scene coordinates to 2D image coordinates, serving as the foundation for differentiable rendering in Gaussian Splatting.

This family replaces or augments the standard perspective projection of 3D Gaussian Splatting to support specific optical characteristics, such as defocus blur or fisheye distortion, or to optimize computational efficiency for specific domains like satellite imagery.

It sets itself apart from standard 3DGS by modifying the projection function $\phi$ and its Jacobian, thereby altering how 2D covariances are derived and how depth-dependent effects (like Circle of Confusion) are modeled.
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of mapping 3D Gaussian primitives $\mathcal{S}$ to 2D screen space for rasterization.
The standard perspective projection model was introduced in the original 3D Gaussian Splatting paper [Kerbl et al., 2023].
Differentiable DOF rendering and Fisheye-GS are extensions developed to handle specific optical phenomena not covered by the standard pinhole camera model.
